extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense / Navy contracting officers, contract negotiators, procurement policy staff, and others implementing OMB Circular A-76 CITA cost-comparison procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, observed practices, evaluative standards, and recommendations for Contracting Officers carrying out cost comparisons and procurements under OMB Circular A-76 for Commercial Industrial Type Activities (CITA). Focuses on solicitation/evaluation/award cycles, treatment of the Government in-house estimate, and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government as another offerer for solicitation amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If solicitation amendments are required for any reason, the Government should be treated exactly as another offerer. Procedures should be established to include the Task Group Chairperson on the distribution for all amendments to solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees indicated it's extremely unlikely they'd negotiate directly with the Government; pre-award/pre-proposal conferences may necessitate changes. Establish distribution procedures to include Task Group Chairperson so amendments are handled like other offerors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Route clarifications through Task Group Chairperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for 'Clarifications' or similar questions, even if Formal Advertising is used, must be referred to the Task Group Chairperson through the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Task Group awareness and preserves integrity of comparison; prevents ad-hoc direct exchanges that could distort the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure in-house estimate reflects solicitation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number of changes to the original solicitation becomes numerous, the Contracting Officer must assure the Government in-house cost estimate reflects these changes to preserve the integrity of the entire comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to update in-house estimate may result in an 'apples and oranges' comparison between Government and contractor concepts of required performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price competition conditions (DAR four-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: For price competition to exist the DAR states four conditions must be met: (1) At least two responsible offerors, (2) who can satisfy the requirements, (3) independently contend for a contract to be awarded to the responsive, responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price, (4) by submitting priced offers responsive to expressed requirements of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If price-competition definition is used, the Government may be characterized as an offeror; use these specific conditions to determine whether price competition exists for cost-comparison decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize Government as competitor when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the definition of competition is restricted to price competition, there should be little to preclude the Government from being considered a competitor; use characterization accordingly in CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize Government's dual role as buyer and seller but treat it as an 'independent seller' relative to private sellers when applying the price-competition test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibility to determine 'contract price' (line 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the specific responsibility of the Contracting Officer to enter the 'Contract Price' on line 10 of the cost comparison form; together with the Government in-house cost estimate this forms the basis for commencement of the actual cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many contracting personnel were unsure of correct figures for various pricing arrangements; Contracting Officers must be familiar with methodologies for different contract types and exercise independent judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm fixed-price evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm fixed-price arrangements: the price of the low offerer or bidder will be entered as the 'contract price' on line 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook silent on whether to include payment discounts; since discounts (e.g., early payment) reduce total Government costs and are used as evaluation criteria, recommendations have been made to include them in the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-price with economic price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: No definitive guidance exists for fixed-price contracts with economic price adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers may need to use best judgment including recent price trends, indices, or other methodologies to determine a fair and reasonable price for cost-comparison purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed-Price Incentive (FPIF) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price Incentive pricing arrangements (e.g., FPIF) are to be evaluated based on the target price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There was debate whether the ceiling rather than the target should be used; unions favored maximum potential liability. Current practice/handbook guidance favors target price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other fixed-price types (successive targets/redetermination) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Other fixed-price arrangements including Fixed-Price Incentive-Successive Targets, Fixed-Price with Redetermination Retroactive and Prospective are not mentioned in the handbook and are unlikely to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixed-Price with Redetermination-Retroactive is incompatible with the cost-comparison process because it provides for adjusting contract price after performance; DAR limits its use to small dollar, short-term R&D contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-reimbursement contract evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Reimbursement Contracts must be subjected to meticulous technical and cost evaluation to assure that estimated costs are neither over nor under estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors should be requested to check offerers' estimates to ensure realism; usual price negotiation develops a Government position lower than contractor's; upward price revisions to contractor offers may need to be negotiated to insure equity in the cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPFF and CPIF entries on cost-comparison form
rubrics_metrics.description: Handbook does not clearly indicate what will be entered on line ten for CPFF or CPIF; practice indicated CPFF uses sum of total estimated costs plus fixed fee; CPIF uses target cost combined with target fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document reflects reported practice but highlights lack of definitive handbook instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPAF evaluation: estimate award-fee portion by performance level
rubrics_metrics.description: For Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contracts the performance level comparable to that attributed to Government employees in preparing the Government estimate will be used to estimate the amount of the fee; the 'contract price' shall be the total estimated cost, base fee, and that portion of the total award fee commensurate with the performance level attributed to Government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of appropriate award-fee portion requires consultation with estimators and functional managers but ultimately an informed, independent judgment by the Contracting Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-and-materials / labor-hour evaluation options
rubrics_metrics.description: If Time and Material or Labor Hour type contracts are used, the total estimated cost of performance may be calculated and entered or alternatively comparable rates may be developed and the cost comparison conducted on the basis of rates rather than total costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research did not reveal instances where the rates-based method was used frequently; Contracting Officers must choose appropriate method and document rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer must exercise informed independent judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer must make the determination of what portion of award fee would be appropriate and, in general, be familiar with methodologies for obtaining the 'contract price' for use in the actual cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes consulting estimators, functional managers, auditors and using professional judgment where guidance is silent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust added Government costs as award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: At bid opening or upon completion of negotiations adjustments will be made to reflect other costs to the Government that will be incurred only if a contract is awarded (e.g., transportation, contract administration, Government furnished materials and supplies, contractor use of Government-owned equipment and facilities, standby maintenance costs, Government personnel termination costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs are not evaluation factors but award factors; NAVMAT memorandum provides rationale (they do not determine grasp of requirement, expertise, ranking, competitive range, are not equally applied, and apply only to the otherwise successful bidder).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of evaluation factors versus award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain added costs should be treated as 'award factors' rather than 'evaluation factors' because they are not used to determine an offeror's grasp of the requirement, expertise, ranking, competitive range, are not equally applied to all offerors, and are applied only to the otherwise successful bidder/offeror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat similarly to responsibility determinations and EEO compliances per NAVMAT recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing directives require the sealed in-house cost estimate must be submitted to the Contracting Officer by the required submission date for bids and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researcher found no written guidance on actions if the cost estimate is submitted late; Contracting Officers should monitor closely and may need to extend bid opening to avoid late submission—but automatic extension is controversial as it may favor the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict between late-proposal provisions and Gov estimate treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison clause used in negotiated solicitations indicates the Government in-house cost estimate will be considered a proposal; the provision for late proposals normally rejects late proposals received after the specified receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a conflict with CITA directives that require the in-house estimate; contracting personnel should be aware of this inconsistency and handle late submissions carefully to preserve integrity and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and disclosure of revealing Government in-house estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: For Formally Advertised Procurements the Government cost estimate will be revealed at the bid opening (contractors and union may be provided the estimate at bid opening or as soon as practicable thereafter). For negotiated solicitations clause indicates the estimate is revealed at the conclusion of negotiations at a set time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviewees observed clause coverage is deficient for 8(a) set-asides—existing clause should be modified to indicate the Government in-house estimate will not be revealed for 8(a) negotiated procurements, and attendance of union representatives and interested contracting personnel would not be appropriate in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit inappropriate attendance where disclosure would advantage a party
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance of union representatives or an 8(a) offeror at the opening where the Government in-house estimate would be revealed may compromise integrity as attendees could use the information in subsequent resolicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify clauses and attendance rules for negotiated procurements and 8(a) situations to avoid unfair advantage and inequitable knowledge of Government estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public announcement of preliminary cost-comparison results at bid opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer is responsible for presiding at bid openings and assuring necessary procedures are followed, including making required statements that preliminary calculations indicate either in-house or contract operation provides the most economical method and that final determination will not be made until calculations are verified and responsibility determinations completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to make required public announcement could increase risk of misunderstandings and attacks on system integrity if later errors are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two public review periods and withholding award
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be two review periods: first at bid/public opening and second after the Task Group Decision Summary Recommendation is completed and approved. Award is withheld pending public review a minimum of five workdays (Handbook: 5–15 working days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns exist that five days may be insufficient—mail notification may consume the period; some prefer 15 days for adequate public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and audit of Government cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditing activity conducts review of the cost comparison form; if minor discrepancies are noted the audit certificate is executed; if significant discrepancies are noted they are reported to the Task Group Chairperson with indications of impact and recommendations for correction and resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researcher found no definitive guidance on what constitutes a 'significant discrepancy'—interviewees generally considered it one that altered the relative standing between the low bidder and the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when Government estimate discrepancies cannot be corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: If Government cost estimate cannot be corrected in a timely manner, contracting negotiators suggested possible actions: for new starts the Government estimate will be rejected and a contract awarded; for conversions the solicitation may be cancelled. No requirement was located that cancellation must occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should be familiar with differing requirements for new starts versus conversions and with applicable handbook/direction before taking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals limited; not basis for GAO protest under A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 directives are matters of Executive policy and do not create substantive or procedural rights for GAO protest; appeals process in Section II resolves determinations between in-house and contract performance internally within the agency and decisions are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel should understand the difference between appeal rights (internal, administrative) and GAO protest jurisdiction; failure to comply with Circular is not, by itself, a GAO protest ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preside properly at bid openings to avoid unfair-comparison accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding at bid openings and assuring necessary procedures are followed to avoid any accusation of an unfair comparison is one of the Contracting Officer's responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several personnel were not fully aware of the specific procedural requirements for the 'initial cost comparison' including making preliminary result statements—training and checklist use recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pre-bid / pre-proposal conferences and site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-bid/Pre-proposal Conferences in conjunction with site visits are an important adjunct to the CITA Support Services contracting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps clarify requirements, may necessitate solicitation amendments, and should be managed to preserve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officers must be trained in CITA and cost-comparison process
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract negotiators are in need of additional general training in the CITA program and in the cost comparison process in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to establish dedicated training programs centered on key reference material; Contracting Officers should review organizational/staffing structures and consider dedicated service branches or contract administration branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject inadequate statements of work (SOWs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should reject statements of work that are not adequate for solicitation purposes and require resubmission rather than attempting to correct and update them after receipt in the contracting office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal milestones should be established and milestone integrity maintained; active early management by the Contracting Officer is best to ensure adequate SOWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational solicitations insufficient alone to show commercial interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations by themselves are not a satisfactory method for making a decision to retain a function in-house due to lack of private sector interest; if no commercial interest is expressed via informational solicitation, Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices are still required before deciding to retain performance in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFPP should provide more definitive guidance on what constitutes a sufficient CBD response; in the interim Contracting Officers should be hesitant to rely solely on informational solicitations to avoid unnecessarily extending the acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop multifunctional/combined solicitations where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers should play a more active role in the development of multifunctional solicitations and take the lead in development of a single solicitation document for the same CITA at different organizations to lower acquisition and contract administration costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers must balance advantages of combining requirements (lower costs) against policy of supporting small/disadvantaged businesses; active early coordination with supported organizations recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define procuring command responsibilities to develop expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command and Naval Facilities Engineering Command should definitize agreements as to which command will procure a specific service function to assist in development of specialized expertise at contracting offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified responsibilities enhance coordination, preparation, and submission of statements of work and implementation of CITA procurements.
